psoralen-puva-bergamot-oil-tanning.text: Psoralen and bergamot oil were used in tanning products because the compound makes skin respond more strongly to UVA, so users could darken faster. It is used medically as PUVA for skin conditions; its tanning use has been restricted, and its cosmetic tanning effect is documented mainly from that older use.

nasal-tanning-spray.text: Users buy nasal sprays as a needle-free way to get melanotan-style darkening without lying in the sun. The peptides involved are studied in injected form for pigment, while the nasal route for tanning has no published study.

sunbed-mt2-stack.text: Users combine tanning-bed sessions with melanotan II to build a deep tan in fewer sessions than either alone. Each part is known to darken skin by itself, but the combination has not been trialled and rests on user reports.

primer-tan-base-tan.text: People get a primer or base tan before a trip so they arrive already bronzed and, they hope, burn less. The tan itself is a visible result of UV exposure; the protection it gives has been measured as modest, around SPF 3.

chain: Red or near-infrared light on skin
red-light-tan-myth.text: Some looksmaxxing and skincare posters say red-light devices before sun or bed sessions prime skin to tan more readily. The idea rests on informal reasoning, and no published study of it turned up.

tan-lines-meta.text: Users manage tan lines on purpose, either evening them out for a seamless bronze look or showing them off as a style detail. The result is immediately visible; it is a presentation choice with no clinical research behind it.

chain: Vitamin D forms and pigment rises
vitamin-d-uvb-for-tan.text: Some people frame UVB sun exposure as serving two goals at once: vitamin D production and a tan. UVB is known to drive both, and the entry separates the two aims since each is pursued for different reasons.

tanning-oil.text: Users apply tanning oil while sunbathing to deepen colour and give skin a glossy bronzed finish. The tan comes from sun exposure, and oils have been used for this since the 1920s; sunless DHA oils give colour without UV.

tanning-drops-isle-of-paradise-style.text: Users mix self-tan drops into their moisturiser to choose how deep and how gradual a tan looks, building colour over days. The colour change is visible within hours; there is no independent research on the drops as a format.

tanning-wipes-towelettes.text: Users reach for tanning wipes for a quick, portable way to add bronzed colour without a mitt or bottle. The colour shows up as it develops and is temporary; no clinical trials of the wipes are published.

body-makeup-leg-makeup.text: Users apply body or leg makeup to even out skin tone, cover marks and add colour for a photo or event. The effect is visible immediately and washes off with soap and water, so it is used as a same-day look.

tan-extender-moisturizer.text: Users apply tan-extender lotions to keep a self-tan looking fresh for longer than the usual 3 to 10 days, and some formulas add a little DHA to top up colour. The slower-fade claim is untested; the DHA top-up gives visible colour.

exfoliating-before-tanning.text: Users scrub before applying self-tanner so colour goes on smoothly and avoids patches or streaks. The rationale follows how DHA reacts in the dead outer layer of skin; the routine is widely recommended in tanning guides but has no trials.

instagram-tan-filter-photo-editing.text: Users edit or filter photos to appear tanner, warming and deepening skin tone in the image without any sun or product. The change is visible immediately in the picture, as part of the wider trend of social media beauty filters.

sunless-tan-injections-tan-jabs.text: Users inject melanotan, a synthetic alpha-MSH analogue, to darken skin with less or no sun exposure. Its pigment-raising action is established; the tanning use itself is unlicensed, and health agencies have issued warnings since 2007.

chain: Pigment deposits in skin and fat
tanning-gummies-supplements.text: Tanning gummies and pills are marketed to deepen a tan using carotenoids such as beta-carotene. Older canthaxanthin pills were known to give a golden-orange tint; modern gummies are sold for tanning without approval for that purpose.

chain: Timed UV bed or booth session
indoor-tanning-salon-sessions.text: Users book salon sessions for a controllable, year-round tan from lamps emitting mostly UVA with some UVB. The tanning response to UV is well established; the practice is classed as a carcinogen by the WHO's cancer agency.

heliotherapy-sunlamp.text: Home sunlamps were sold for cosmetic tanning and for skin therapy, and some people still use them for a tan. Clinical versions are used for psoriasis, eczema and vitiligo; research on the cosmetic use focuses mainly on skin cancer risk.

intense-pulsed-light-ipl-photofacial.text: Users get IPL photofacials in clinics to fade sun spots, redness and thread veins for a clearer, more even complexion. It is an established clinic technology for these targets, with tunable filters; home devices are mostly sold for hair removal.

chain: Fewer dark spots, more even tone
q-switched-picosecond-laser-for-pigment.text: Users seek Q-switched or picosecond lasers in clinics to break up sun spots, melasma and tattoo ink for a more even complexion. They are established for tattoo removal and pigmented lesions, with limited published trial detail for cosmetic pigment use.

chemical-peels-tca-jessner.text: Medium-depth peels with TCA, Jessner's solution or glycolic acid are used by clinicians for photoaging, wrinkles, pigment and acne scars, aiming for fresher, smoother skin. They are an established dermatology procedure; DIY versions circulate in appearance forums.

hydroquinone-tretinoin-steroid-triple-cr.text: This prescription triple cream is used to fade melasma and dark patches for a more even face. It is the best-studied topical for melasma, with most trials run on the branded product Tri-Luma.

thiamidol.text: Thiamidol is used in over-the-counter serums to fade dark spots, post-inflammatory marks and melasma. Several trials at 0.2% in melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation exist, though most are industry-linked.

licorice-root-extract-glabridin.text: Licorice extract is used in brightening products to lighten dark spots and even out tone. Glabridin blocks tyrosinase in cell studies, and no human pigment trials were located for the appearance use.

vitamin-e-ferulic-acid.text: Ferulic acid with vitamin C and E is a serum staple used for brightening and anti-aging. Its antioxidant activity is documented in lab work, while human brightening trials were not located.

chain: Citrus acid and vitamin C applied
lemon-juice-on-skin.text: Lemon juice is a folk remedy people apply to lighten dark spots, freckles and marks. The idea rests on citrus acidity and vitamin C, with no trials behind it.

cica-centella-asiatica.text: Cica creams and serums, made from the gotu kola plant, are used to calm skin and help marks recover after blemishes. The herb has a long traditional use as a soothing agent; trials for pigment recovery were not located.

oral-cysteine-nac-for-pigment.text: Some people in skin-lightening circles take NAC or cysteine hoping that raising glutathione will lighten pigment. NAC has established medical uses, and pigment studies for this appearance goal were not located.

sun-avoidance-hat-protocol.text: Users add shade, wide-brimmed hats and protective clothing on top of sunscreen to keep melasma from returning and to slow visible skin ageing. Sun is a documented trigger for both; hat protocols themselves have not been tested.

sunscreen-vitamin-c-layering-routine.text: Users apply a vitamin C serum under sunscreen each morning as a brightening and anti-aging routine. The rationale is plausible given each product's known role, but the pairing itself has not been trialled.
